query: Our iOS app renders a completely blank home screen whenever the ranking service or the image CDN has a wobble - not a degraded feed, nothing at all, and the client logs just say `data` was null. The rest of the backend is healthy at the time. Read feed-schema.graphql and tell me why this happens and exactly what to change.
expected_behavior: Names the mechanism: an execution error on a Non-Null position propagates to the parent response position, and because every position from `Query.viewer` down to `Post.relevanceScore` / `Image` is non-null, the error keeps bubbling until the whole `data` entry is null

States that GraphQL fields are nullable by default deliberately, so that a single failing or unauthorised field degrades to null instead of failing the request, and that `!` is a promise the server has to keep - not a convenience for the client's generated types

Fixes it by making the positions that can fail independently nullable - `relevanceScore`, `heroImage`, `billingSummary`, and the `viewer` / `post` root fields - rather than by adding try/catch or fallback values in every resolver

Points out that `[Post!]!` means one bad element nulls the entire list (and then the non-null list nulls its parent), so the item non-null inside a fallible list is the risky part, not the list non-null
Rejects the premise that non-null everywhere is good for the generated client types, and says the client should handle nullable fields (optional chaining / no force-unwrap) instead
Does not recommend `@experimental_disableErrorPropagation` or a `null`-bubbling opt-out as the primary fix, or if it mentions such an option, flags it as non-standard and implementation-specific

query: Reviewers keep complaining that our catalogue paging is wrong: shoppers see duplicated and skipped products while stock updates land, and `page: 9000` times out. Rework the pagination in catalog-schema.graphql and give me the SDL plus the resolver rules.
expected_behavior: Replaces page/pageSize with a cursor Connection: `products(first: Int, after: String, last: Int, before: String): ProductConnection!` plus `edges { node cursor }` and `pageInfo { hasNextPage hasPreviousPage startCursor endCursor }`
Explains why offset paging produces duplicates and gaps - the offset is recomputed against a list that shifted between requests - and that large offsets force the database to count and discard rows

Says the cursor must be opaque to the client (base64-encoded, documented as unstable) and must encode the sort key plus a tiebreaker such as the id, so the underlying query becomes a keyset/seek predicate rather than an offset
Requires a default page size and a server-enforced maximum, and says an out-of-range `first` should be a request error rather than silently clamped or unbounded
Keeps `totalCount` nullable or off the connection, or calls out that an exact count is a separate expensive query, instead of leaving `totalCount: Int!` on every page
Notes that `reviews` and `variants` are unbounded lists that need the same treatment (or an explicit justification that they are bounded)
Mentions that the Connection shape comes from the Relay cursor connections specification rather than from the GraphQL specification itself

query: A single home-feed request fires several hundred SQL statements and one HTTP call to the ranking service per post. Go through feed-resolvers.js and give me the corrected version.
expected_behavior: Flags the module-level `authorLoader` as the most serious bug: a loader shared across requests caches rows for the lifetime of the process, so it serves stale data and leaks one user's authorised rows into another user's request - loaders must be constructed per request and put on the context

Points out that the existing batch function is broken even as a batch function, because it returns whatever order Postgres gave back and drops missing ids, while DataLoader requires an array of exactly `keys.length` results in the same order as `keys` (with `null` or an `Error` for misses)

Adds loaders for the remaining per-row resolvers - `Post.comments`, `Post.likeCount`, `Author.followerCount`, `Author.posts` - noting that list-valued relationships batch to one grouped query keyed by the parent id
Batches `relevanceScore` into a single ranking-service call for the whole feed rather than one call per post
Says `Post.likeCount` and `Author.followerCount` should be aggregated in one grouped `count(*) ... GROUP BY` query (or a counter column), not counted per row
Recommends a verification step that counts the statements a real feed query issues, rather than asserting the fix works

Adds demand control - depth, breadth/alias and complexity limits, and pagination on `Viewer.feed`, `Post.comments` and `Author.posts` - because `Post.author.posts.author...` is cyclical and batching alone does not bound it

query: Product wants four changes to checkout-schema.graphql: `shippingCountry` should become an ISO country code enum, `placeOrder` should stop throwing on bad coupons and report them properly, `orders` needs a `status` filter, and `PENDING` should be renamed to `AWAITING_PAYMENT`. Two partner integrations cannot be upgraded on our schedule. Tell me how to land each one and what the rollout looks like.
expected_behavior: Classifies each change as breaking or additive instead of treating them uniformly: changing a field's type and renaming an enum value are breaking, adding an optional argument is safe, and reworking the mutation result is breaking unless done as a new field

Handles the country change additively - add a new `shippingCountryCode: CountryCode` field alongside the old one and mark the old field `@deprecated(reason: ...)` - rather than retyping the existing field

Says a new enum value is safe to add for output positions but that removing or renaming one is breaking, and handles `PENDING` by adding `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, deprecating `PENDING`, and keeping the old value served until traffic on it is zero

Warns that adding an enum value is a breaking change for input positions and for clients that switch exhaustively, and tells clients to keep a default branch and to query `__typename` on unions/interfaces

Moves the coupon and stock failures out of thrown top-level errors into errors-as-data - a `placeOrderV2`-style payload with the order plus a typed `userErrors` list (or a result union) - and keeps genuine infrastructure failures in the top-level `errors` array

Points out that adding a required argument or input field (non-null with no default) is breaking, so the `status` filter must be an optional argument (nullable or defaulted) with no new required input fields

Bases removal on measured per-field usage over a deprecation window rather than on a fixed number of releases, and names a mechanised breaking-change check (schema diff in CI, e.g. `graphql-inspector diff`, or the federation equivalent) as the gate
Does not propose a URL/header API version such as `/graphql/v2` as the primary strategy

query: Design the pagination and the error response format for this REST endpoint and write the result up as an OpenAPI 3.1 document. The 500 on a bad coupon and the 200 on create are both wrong.
expected_behavior: Answers as REST/HTTP contract design: correct status codes (201 with `Location` on create, 4xx for client faults), a documented pagination scheme with links or cursors, and an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` error body, written as an OpenAPI 3.1 document
Does not propose a GraphQL schema, Connection/edges/pageInfo shapes, resolvers or a `userErrors` payload for what is an HTTP endpoint

query: Our home feed comes back as `feed: null` every time the ranking service hiccups. The schema is code-first in feed-builder.ts (Pothos 4). A teammate says the cause is that Pothos makes every field non-null by default, and wants to add `nullable: true` to every field in the file. Is that right? Tell me what SDL this file actually generates and what the smallest correct fix is.
expected_behavior: Rejects the teammate's premise: in Pothos 4 output fields are nullable by default and only `nullable: false` makes one non-null, so adding `nullable: true` everywhere changes nothing for most fields

Gives the generated SDL correctly for the fields that matter: `relevanceScore: Float!`, `id: ID!`, `title: String!`, `heroImage: Image` (nullable), `tags: [String!]`, and `feed(first: Int): [Post!]` - i.e. the list is nullable but its items are non-null

Explains the chain: the ranking error at the explicitly non-null `relevanceScore` propagates to its `Post`, and because Pothos list items default to non-null the failing `Post` nulls the entire `feed` list
Proposes a targeted fix - remove `nullable: false` from `relevanceScore`, and/or make the feed items nullable with `nullable: { list: ..., items: true }` - rather than a blanket `nullable: true`

Recommends checking the printed SDL (`printSchema(builder.toSchema())` or the committed generated SDL) or reproducing with the ranking service failing, rather than reasoning from the builder calls alone

query: Review pr-order-input.graphql before I merge it. The reviewer on the PR says every non-null field or argument we add to a shipped schema is a breaking change, so all three new `PlaceOrderInput` fields and `includeArchived` have to move into a `PlaceOrderInputV2` / `ordersV2`. Our old mobile clients (operations at the bottom of the file) cannot be force-upgraded. Which of these additions actually break those clients, and what should the PR change?
expected_behavior: Says `currency: CurrencyCode! = USD` and `includeArchived: Boolean! = false` do not break the old clients: an argument or input field is required only when it is non-null and has no default, so documents that omit them still validate and the resolver receives the default

Identifies `channel: SalesChannel!` (non-null, no default) as the one breaking addition - the old `PlaceOrder` variables omit it and fail validation - and fixes it by making it nullable or giving it a default rather than versioning the whole input
Classifies `giftMessage: String` as a safe additive change
Rejects the blanket `PlaceOrderInputV2` / `ordersV2` as unnecessary for the defaulted and nullable additions

Notes that a default is a behavioural contract: every old client now implicitly sends `USD` and `false`, so the default must equal today's behaviour (schema-diff tools flag such additions as dangerous rather than breaking)
Verifies with a mechanised check - `graphql-inspector diff` between the shipped and the PR schema, or validating the old operations against the new schema - rather than asserting the result
